details: Technical discussions between the U.S. and Iran took place in Doha on July 1st, mediated by Qatar, to address shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and a lasting ceasefire. Key issues include Iran's demand for control and fees for passage, opposed by the U.S. and Gulf states. Iran also seeks the release of frozen assets. No direct meetings occurred, and Iranian clerics reportedly threatened former US President Trump. This ongoing tension in a critical shipping lane could impact global trade and energy markets.
title: US, Iran Hold Indirect Talks on Strait of Hormuz and Frozen Assets

details: Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Kyiv on July 2nd, resulting in at least 21 deaths and over 80 injuries. Damage was reported in 30 locations, mostly residential buildings. This escalation in the conflict highlights ongoing geopolitical instability in Eastern Europe and its potential impact on global energy markets and investor confidence.
title: Russia Unleashes Massive Attack on Kyiv, 21 Dead

details: Former US President Donald Trump's financial disclosures reveal over $2.2 billion in income during his first year back in office, with $1.4 billion originating from his family's crypto business, World Liberty Financial. This boom is attributed to loosened regulations under his administration. Additionally, Trump flew on a new Air Force One, a $400 million gift from Qatar, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest.
title: Trump's $2.2 Billion Income Includes $1.4B from Crypto Business

details: Oil prices have fallen to levels not seen since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, with Brent crude dropping below $71 a barrel. This decline follows reports of encouraging progress in indirect technical talks between the U.S. and Iran in Doha, aimed at securing a lasting ceasefire and resolving issues related to the Strait of Hormuz. Reduced geopolitical tensions in the Middle East could ease global energy supply concerns.
title: Oil Prices Decline on Progress in US-Iran Peace Talks
